newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banacci higher again on sales rumours.
newsitem.headline: Banacci higher again on sales rumours.

text.p: Shares of Banamex-Accival (Banacci) rose sharply for a second successive day Thursday in speculative buying with the financial group rumoured to be interested in offloading an Argentine asset, traders said.

Banacci officials were not available for comment on the company's rumoured plans to sell part or all of its holding in Banesto-Banco Shaw. Banacci acquired a 57 percent stake in Banesto-Banco Shaw along with Banco del Sud in 1994.
Nonetheless, the group's shares were up and analysts said the sale would have notable advantages.

Banacci A class shares bucked a general downward trend among Mexican stocks at midday trade on Thursday, gaining 46 centavos to 16.60 pesos and that after rising 1.04 pesos to 16.14 pesos on Wednesday.

"They're not buying as heavily as yesterday, in fact the B series is down on profit-taking, like the market in general. Nonetheless, the A and L series are still doing well. Rumors about the Argentine sale persist," a desk trader said.
The Bear Stearns brokerage referred to the rumored sale in its daily Latin America Watch report on Thursday.
The report noted the sale, should it come about, would be one way for Banacci to raise capital without diluting shares.

Banacci committed itself on Jan 23 to raising some four billion pesos (approximately $500 million) in capital in return for offloading some eight billion pesos in past-due loans onto the Mexican government.

"For Banamex, such a transaction will be very positive since it will complete a big chunk of its capitalization program without dilution. Last week, Banamex's top management went to Argentina," the Bear Stearns said.
